$ stk 
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
stk — supertoolkit

  stk init                    create the local CA and a starter supertoolkit.yaml
  stk add <service>...        add services, with safe default policy
  stk connect <service>       store a credential, read from stdin
  stk connect <service> --device
                              connect with no browser on this machine (RFC 8628)
  stk connect <service> --browser
                              connect via OAuth 2.0 authorization code + PKCE
  stk handover key|seal|open  move a credential to a broker that has no browser
  stk run -- <command>        run a command with the broker in front of it
  stk serve                   run the broker daemon on a Unix socket
  stk serve --proxy-listen <loopback host:port>
                              also keep the egress proxy on a fixed port, key required
  stk reload [--json]         re-read supertoolkit.yaml into the running serve (also SIGHUP)
  stk env [--json]            print the proxy URL, CA and placeholders for that proxy
  stk mcp [--profile <p>]     speak MCP on stdio, four meta-tools
  stk mcp serve <server> [--profile <p>] [--socket <path>] [--standalone]
                              serve one fronted MCP server's own tools, each call
                              decided and audited, its egress through the broker
  stk install --user <name>    run stk as its own OS user under systemd (Linux)
  stk mcp install <host>       print the client configuration (no secret in it)
  stk verify <service> [--expect-login <login>] [--json]
                              prove a stored credential works, and as whom
  stk revoke <service> [--local]
                              withdraw a credential, here and at the provider
  stk audit [--limit n] [--json]
                              what the broker actually did, newest first
  stk approvals [allow|refuse <id>]
                              what is waiting on you, and decide it
  stk publish submit|perform <id>|recover
                              durable SuperPipeline-gated automatic X publishing
  stk ui [--bind addr] [--no-open]
                              the five screens, on a one-time link
  stk doctor                  check the setup, and prove no credential leaks
  stk doctor --probe          prove each client here actually goes through the broker
                              (exit 1 on a bypass; --json for a machine-readable list;
                              --with-proxy-key probes through a keyed broker)
  stk doctor --json [--agent-uid <uid>]...  checks and the isolation verdict as JSON
  stk version

The agent never holds a credential. Known services: aws-sts, cloudflare, github, github-app, google, notion, openai, resend, slack, stripe, superpipeline-approvals-read, superpipeline-approvals-write, x

stk — supertoolkit

  stk init                    create the local CA and a starter supertoolkit.yaml

  stk connect <service>       store a credential, read from stdin

  stk connect <service> --browser

  stk handover key|seal|open  move a credential to a broker that has no browser
  stk run -- <command>        run a command with the broker in front of it
  stk serve                   run the broker daemon on a Unix socket
  stk serve --proxy-listen <loopback host:port>
                              also keep the egress proxy on a fixed port, key required
  stk reload [--json]         re-read supertoolkit.yaml into the running serve (also SIGHUP)
  stk env [--json]            print the proxy URL, CA and placeholders for that proxy
  stk mcp [--profile <p>]     speak MCP on stdio, four meta-tools
  stk mcp serve <server> [--profile <p>] [--socket <path>] [--standalone]
                              serve one fronted MCP server's own tools, each call
                              decided and audited, its egress through the broker
  stk install --user <name>    run stk as its own OS user under systemd (Linux)
  stk mcp install <host>       print the client configuration (no secret in it)
  stk verify <service> [--expect-login <login>] [--json]
                              prove a stored credential works, and as whom
  stk revoke <service> [--local]
                              withdraw a credential, here and at the provider
  stk audit [--limit n] [--json]
                              what the broker actually did, newest first
  stk approvals [allow|refuse <id>]
                              what is waiting on you, and decide it
  stk publish submit|perform <id>|recover
                              durable SuperPipeline-gated automatic X publishing

                              the five screens, on a one-time link

  stk doctor --probe          prove each client here actually goes through the broker
                              (exit 1 on a bypass; --json for a machine-readable list;
                              --with-proxy-key probes through a keyed broker)
  stk doctor --json [--agent-uid <uid>]...  checks and the isolation verdict as JSON
  stk version

stk — supertoolkit

  stk init                    create the local CA and a starter supertoolkit.yaml
  stk add <service>...        add services, with safe default policy
  stk connect <service>       store a credential, read from stdin
  stk connect <service> --device
                              connect with no browser on this machine (RFC 8628)
  stk connect <service> --browser
                              connect via OAuth 2.0 authorization code + PKCE
  stk handover key|seal|open  move a credential to a broker that has no browser
  stk run -- <command>        run a command with the broker in front of it
  stk serve                   run the broker daemon on a Unix socket
  stk serve --proxy-listen <loopback host:port>
                              also keep the egress proxy on a fixed port, key required
  stk reload [--json]         re-read supertoolkit.yaml into the running serve (also SIGHUP)
  stk env [--json]            print the proxy URL, CA and placeholders for that proxy
  stk mcp [--profile <p>]     speak MCP on stdio, four meta-tools
  stk mcp serve <server> [--profile <p>] [--socket <path>] [--standalone]
                              serve one fronted MCP server's own tools, each call
                              decided and audited, its egress through the broker
  stk install --user <name>    run stk as its own OS user under systemd (Linux)
  stk mcp install <host>       print the client configuration (no secret in it)
  stk verify <service> [--expect-login <login>] [--json]
                              prove a stored credential works, and as whom
  stk revoke <service> [--local]
                              withdraw a credential, here and at the provider
  stk audit [--limit n] [--json]
                              what the broker actually did, newest first
  stk approvals [allow|refuse <id>]
                              what is waiting on you, and decide it
  stk publish submit|perform <id>|recover
                              durable SuperPipeline-gated automatic X publishing
  stk ui [--bind addr] [--no-open]
                              the five screens, on a one-time link
  stk doctor                  check the setup, and prove no credential leaks
  stk doctor --probe          prove each client here actually goes through the broker
                              (exit 1 on a bypass; --json for a machine-readable list;
                              --with-proxy-key probes through a keyed broker)
  stk doctor --json [--agent-uid <uid>]...  checks and the isolation verdict as JSON
  stk version

$ stk serve --bogus

stk: serve: unknown argument "--bogus" (usage: stk serve [--proxy-listen <loopback host:port>] [--allow-uid <n>]... [--socket-mode 0600|0660] [--local-commands-socket <absolute path>] [--local-commands-mode 0600|0660])


$ stk serve --proxy-listen
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
stk: --proxy-listen needs a loopback host:port


$ stk serve --proxy-listen 0.0.0.0:8899
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
stk: --proxy-listen "0.0.0.0:8899": only loopback addresses (127.0.0.0/8, ::1) are accepted; 0.0.0.0 is reachable from other machines


$ stk serve --proxy-listen 127.0.0.1:0
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
stk: --proxy-listen "127.0.0.1:0": port 0 picks a random port; a fixed proxy needs a fixed one


$ stk serve --proxy-listen=localhost:x
exit 1

--- stderr
stk: --proxy-listen "localhost:x": "x" is not a port number

$ stk handover key
exit 0
--- stdout
$HANDOVER_KEY
--- stderr

  this broker's hand-over key. It is public: it can only seal, never open.

  on a machine that has a browser, with stk installed there:
    stk connect <service>            # or however you obtain the credential
    stk handover seal <service> --to '<the key above>'

  what this path costs, plainly: the credential exists on that machine for as
  long as it takes to seal it. The device flow and the web UI do not have that
  property, so prefer them when either is possible.


$ stk handover key --json
exit 0
--- stdout
{"public_key":"$HANDOVER_KEY"}
--- stderr


$ stk handover seal github --to
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
stk: --to needs the broker's hand-over key, from `stk handover key`


$ stk handover seal github --to not-a-key
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
stk: that is not a supertoolkit hand-over key


$ stk handover seal github --to $HANDOVER_KEY
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
stk: github is not connected here, so there is nothing to seal: no credential stored for "github": run `stk connect github`


$ stk handover seal github --stdin --to $HANDOVER_KEY  <<< "ghp_characterization_fixture"
exit 0
--- stdout
$SEALED_ENVELOPE
--- stderr

  sealed to that broker and to nothing else. Pipe it there:
    stk handover open github

  it is safe in a paste buffer, a chat message or a file: only the broker
  holding the matching private key can open it. The credential it carries,
  however, still exists on this machine — in this store.


$ stk handover open github  <<< "not an envelope"
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
stk: that is not a supertoolkit hand-over envelope
